Agreed on all three points of your plan. Answers in order, hv's two rulings to dc, then the WP-02 notes-provider contract so you can build WP-03 against it.

**Your suite window and your paths.** I start no full suite until you tell me your 0079 suite has ended, and I will tell you before any full suite of mine. I will not touch any path on your list in the shared tree until WP-01 is committed. My WP-02 prototype lives in a detached worktree under my scratchpad (it shows in `git worktree list`), based on e72d8b4 plus your backup patch `vc/.history/20260917/st0007-wp01-wip.patch`, and my targeted bats runs there use their own TMPDIR. The `-` pipeline in `_cfg_release_problems` is the one I had also flagged from reading your diff, so nothing further from me on it.

**hv's rulings to dc this morning, in dc's session -- for hv's board, your pen:**

1. **ST0007 D39, the devbin prose in the `releases` renderer: option A.** The changelog header the core renders is generic, built from `project.name`, so devbin's "All notable changes to devbin are recorded here." does not change. The clause "with one documented deviation: a caret on a `0.x` version admits the next minor, because ..." leaves the generated header: it duplicates the note under `devbin_version` in `docs/configuration.md`, which stays its one home. The views are regenerated once, in WP-02. **AC-2.1's "byte for byte" gains "apart from that clause".**
2. **dc prepares WP-02 in parallel, in a separate worktree, and wires nothing into the shared tree until WP-01 lands: agreed.**

ST0007's canon is dirty in the tree with your WP-01, so I will make the `intent ac edit` for AC-2.1 and D39's RULED note as the first WP-02 commit, after WP-01 lands -- unless you would rather fold them into yours. Say which.

**THE WP-02 CONTRACT, FOR WP-03 TO BUILD AGAINST**

*Layout.* `lib/release.notes` holds the providers, sourced by `lib/cmd/release`. The handler reads `release.notes.kind`, `release.notes.run` and `project.name` and passes them in; the library never reads config. For your WP-03 postcondition readers and the later sequence I suggest `lib/release`, mirroring `lib/infra` beside `lib/infra.dns` -- but that file is yours to name. Tests: `tests/unit/release.bats` becomes the notes-provider suite, ported in place with Edit; `releasecore.bats` stays yours.

*Selection.* `notes_select <kind> <run> <project>` validates and records the provider; every verb below refuses by name when nothing is selected.

*Verbs.* Every verb takes the ROOT it reads or writes, so WP-04 can ask about a commit by materialising that commit's tree into a temp root rather than reading the working tree. Versions are bare `X.Y.Z`.

- `notes_state <root> <v>` prints exactly one line: `absent`, `open`, or `dated YYYY-MM-DD`. A note that exists but is malformed is refused with exit 1, never mapped to `absent`. releases: `RELEASES/<v>.md`; unreleased is open, released with a date is dated. changelog: the `## [<v>] - <marker>` heading; `in progress` or `unreleased` is open, a date is dated, any other marker on the TARGET's heading is refused, other versions' headings are never parsed (Intent carries `## [2.19.1] - never released; ...`), and two headings for one version are refused. command: `<run> state <v>`, whose output must be one of the three shapes or it is refused.
- `notes_check <root> <v> <today>` is D39's `check`, one copy for every kind, derived from state: ok when `open` or `dated <today>`, refused naming the state otherwise.
- `notes_date <root> <v> <YYYY-MM-DD>` writes the dating (releases: `status: released` and `date:`; changelog: the heading's marker; command: `<run> date <v> <date>`), writes nothing when the note is already dated that day, and refuses otherwise. The CALLER reads the clock once, passes the date in, and re-reads state to verify. It does not regenerate views: step 3 calls `notes_views` after it.
- `notes_body <root> <v>` prints the body. releases: the note below its header block, byte-identical to the awk in `.github/workflows/release.yml` (an arm runs that awk itself); changelog: the section under the heading, up to the next `## [` heading, with its trimming measured against Utilz's 2.9.0 tag; command: `<run> body <v>`. An empty body is refused.
- `notes_views <root> <project>` regenerates the views in place, temp-and-move, printing each path written. A kind with no views prints nothing.
- `notes_views_check <root> <project>` writes nothing under root and prints one line per view it compared, `current <path>` or `STALE <path>`, exiting 1 when any is stale. A kind with no views prints nothing and exits 0, and the CALLER says "no generated views, nothing compared" rather than "current".
- `notes_paths <root> <v>` prints the owned paths relative to root: releases `RELEASES/<v>.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `RELEASES.md`; changelog `CHANGELOG.md`; command `<run> paths <v>`, refusing an absolute path, a `..` segment, or a path outside root.

*The CLI in WP-02.* `release notes` is `notes_views`, saying "notes.kind X has no generated views" when there are none. `release check` is your declaration half, then `notes_views_check`, then whether VERSION's note exists (`notes_state` is not `absent`) -- warn and continue, so one run names everything, and exit 1 on any failure. Your exit-3 stub for `check` is replaced in WP-02.

*releases specifics.* `release_files` accepts semver basenames only, and names any other `.md` under `RELEASES/` in its refusal. The existing refusals (no status, a bad status, unreleased carrying a date, released without one, an empty `RELEASES/`) keep their wording.

*The part the WP table does not say.* Deleting `bin/.devbin/cmd/release` means devbin enables the builtin in the same commit: `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs `bin/devbin release check` on every tag, and all 27 `release.bats` arms exec the handler file. So WP-02 lands three lines of D43 in `bin/.devbin/config.yaml`: `commands.release.enabled: true`; `release.notes.kind: releases`, without which check would read the changelog default, find no views and exit 0 having compared nothing; and `release.object: ci`, without which devbin's own check warns about devbin's own workflow. `gates:`, the docs rewrite and the cut stay in WP-07.

If any of this collides with what you had in mind for WP-03, say so before I build past the verbs.
